correctness.rationale: Proved scalar Schur/Perron threshold without irreducibility; proved a tight per-spoke cost inequality and an exact LP reduction; applied sufficient KKT to a strictly convex quadratic feasible set, including uniqueness and positivity; derived sharp two-spoke reciprocity price bounds and unbounded asymmetric-cost family. Verified rational determinant and exact example with standalone package script. The proof distinguishes non-supercriticality from strict exponential decay.

originality.rationale: The exact paired closed-form global cost minimizers and sharp reciprocal-price dichotomy were not found or implied in the inspected 2026 source or comparable general prior control frameworks. Nonnegative matrix spectral tools, fractional knapsack, and KKT are acknowledged as classical. Closest general prior Zhang–Lu–Pei 2018 controls different variables/costs; plausible unindexed coverage remains a risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed exact arrowhead control optimization might already imply the directional/reciprocal classification.

General geometric programming and convex allocation frameworks may offer alternate derivations for subsets of the result, although the inspected particular theorems have different controlled quantities and costs.
Real reciprocal physical contact constraints depend on population sizes; the model postulates symmetric multiplicative reductions rather than asserting physical bilateral flow equivalence.

value.rationale: For a motivated heterogeneous transmission topology, the theorem completely classifies optimal intervention costs under two operationally distinct feasibility constraints, for all numbers and weights of peripheral groups. The sharp factor-two symmetric price and unbounded asymmetric price show a structurally meaningful and quantitatively consequential difference, not a numerical recomputation or arbitrary parameter slice. Applicability is limited to initial-growth spectral control with linear resource costs.
